source_evidence: D327~15:38 exact player 'I own a large part of a river’s shipping route and security… I think you can imagine the possibilites' continues V's commercial pretext, not an undertaking to commit crime, payment or quantified assertion of actual market control. Mara independently grounds the claim in genuine holdings: 'We have a mill and a private berth, and interests in a bargeyard and a fort. We are interested in what moves along the river as well as what passes through our own hands.' No assertion of monopoly, actual traffic volumes, unverified operating status or authority over public inspections. Tavosk recognizes the potential for a repeat customer and responds voluntarily within his already acknowledged private service, clarifying that he has useful contacts concerning Orsaven berth inspections, not authority over the entire river, and proposes a limited initial fee: 'For a first advance notice concerning an Orsaven berth inspection, six gold pieces. If you want a continuing arrangement, we can discuss that once I understand the traffic you expect.' This is a new prospective offer adjudicated from his own commercial incentives, grounded in the already observed D320 6gp and D323 8gp information-payment precedents; not a retroactive fee schedule, confirmed future inspection, promised immunity, receipt, agreement, specific existing client or guarantee. His earlier partial success remains intact; the offer follows V providing new business context and Mara's truthful clarification, not a reroll or retroactive DC23 success. No contested concession/check needed for the NPC to quote his own tentative terms after his prior admission; no payment, cargo order, signature, unlawful shipment, actual inspection warning or additional disclosure by V. Cirren/Fenar/Mara hear Tavosk personally offer a price. V chooses response, no additional spending or time beyond brief dialogue.
